{{Short description|Irish mathematician (1893–1943)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2021}}
{{Use Irish English|date=May 2019}}
'''Charles Henry Rowe''' (9 February 1893, [[Cork (city)|Cork]]{{snd}}4 December 1943) was an Irish mathematician, specializing in geometry.<ref name=Obit>{{cite journal|author=Semple, J. G.|authorlink=John Greenlees Semple|title=Charles Henry Rowe|journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society|volume=19|issue= 76, Part 4|year=1944|pages=241–244|doi=10.1112/jlms/19.76_Part_4.241}}</ref> He was [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Mathematics]] at [[Trinity College Dublin]] (1926–1943).<ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/about/400Hist/7.php Erasmus Smith's professors of Mathematics] Mathematics at TCD 1592–1992</ref>

==Career==
Rowe received his bachelor's degree from [[University College Cork]] in 1914 and his M.A. in Mathematics and Philosophy from [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1917. He was a close friend of the mathematical physicist [[John Lighton Synge|J. L. Synge]].<ref>{{cite book|editor=McCartney, Mark|editor2=Whitaker, Andrew|title=Physicists of Ireland: passion and precision|publisher=CRC Press|year=2003|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CyXOBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA212|page=212|isbn=9781420033175}}</ref> By winning a competitive examination in 1920, Rowe became a Fellow of Trinity College Dublin and retained the fellowship until his death. He spent the academic year 1920–1921 in Paris, where he studied under [[Jacques Hadamard|Hadamard]], [[Henri Lebesgue|Lebesgue]], and [[Édouard Goursat|Goursat]].{{fact|date=June 2021}}

From 1923 to 1926 he was the [[Donegall Lecturer in Mathematics]] at TCD<ref name=Obit/> and, after a probationary period as an acting professor,<ref>{{cite book|title=The Dublin University Calendar for the Year 1922–1923|page=448|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LQQLAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA448|last1=Trinity College (Dublin|first1=Ireland)|year=1922}}</ref> was appointed in 1926 to the [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Mathematics at Trinity College Dublin|Erasmus Smith's Professor of Mathematics]], retaining the position until his death.<ref name=Obit/>

In 1932 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]], with talk ''Subspaces associated with certain systems of curves in a Riemannian space'', in 1932 in Zurich. The Rowe Prize of Trinity College Dublin was established in 1959 by a bequest from his widow, Olive Marjorie Rowe.<ref>{{cite web|title=Scholarship Prizes and Financial Assistance, School of Mathematics, Trinity College Dublin|url=http://www.maths.tcd.ie/prospective/prizesetc.php}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*"A kinematical treatment of some theorems on normal rectilinear congruences." ''Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 31 (1929) 919–930. {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9947-1929-1501522-4}}
*"On certain doubly infinite systems of curves on a surface." ''Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 36 (1930) 695–704. {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9904-1930-05040-5}}
*"Some theorems on the generators of a hyperboloid." ''Mathematische Annalen'' 103, no. 1 (1930): 516–531. {{doi|10.1007/BF01455707}}
*"A Proof of the Asymptotic Series for log Γ(z) and log Γ(z+ a)." ''Annals of Mathematics'' (1931): 10–16. {{doi|10.2307/1968409}}
*"A characteristic property of systems of paths." In ''Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy''. Section A: Mathematical and Physical Sciences, vol. 40, pp. 99–106. Royal Irish Academy, 1931. {{JSTOR|20490688}}
*"Characteristic properties of certain systems of paths in a Riemannian space." In ''Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy''. Section A: Mathematical and Physical Sciences, vol. 41, pp. 102–110. Royal Irish Academy, 1932. {{JSTOR|20490700}}
*[http://eudml.org/doc/235155 "On certain systems of curves in Riemannian space."] ''Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées'' 12 (1933): 283–308.
*"On natural families of curves." ''Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 39 (1933) 793–801. {{doi|10.1090/S0002-9904-1933-05743-9}}
*with Bertrand Gambier: [http://eudml.org/doc/81527 "Lieu des points dont les rapports des distances à trois droites fixes restent constants: biquadratiques, cubiques gauches et dégénérescences."] In ''Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure'', vol. 53, pp. 329–386. Elsevier, 1936.
*[https://eudml.org/doc/81557 "Couples de tétraèdres de Moebius inscrits dans une quadrique (ou une biquadrique) et circonscrits à une autre quadrique (ou une développable de classe quatre)."] In ''Annales scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure'', vol. 58, pp. 261–283. Elsevier, 1941.
